title: Deterministic Markdown structure and accessibility diagnostics

rules.title: Heading level increases by more than one
rules.interpretation: A navigation and accessibility review cue; some generated or embedded Markdown structures may use deliberate jumps.

rules.title: Heading has no visible text
rules.interpretation: An empty heading usually creates an unusable navigation landmark, but rendered HTML context may change the result.

rules.title: Normalized heading text is repeated
rules.interpretation: Repeated labels can make generated anchors or navigation ambiguous; repetition may still be intentional.

rules.title: Markdown image has empty alternative text
rules.interpretation: Empty alternative text may be correct for a decorative image, so repository and rendered-page context still matter.

limitations: The analyzer reads CommonMark tokens and does not reproduce every hosting platform's Markdown extensions.
Diagnostics identify inspectable properties; they do not measure README usefulness, correctness, or fitness for a specific audience.
Repository links, rendered HTML, and prose semantics are outside this first analyzer.
